subject_area: Computer networks — TCP/IP layered protocol stack
course_intent: Teach the foundational concepts of computer networking through the TCP/IP layered model — students should leave able to explain how data moves across networks layer-by-layer, reason about core protocols (HTTP, TCP, UDP, IP, Ethernet, ARP, DNS), and understand addressing, routing, and basic performance/impairment concepts.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the conceptual + protocol-mechanics level appropriate to a top-down/bottom-up networking fundamentals course. Hands-on socket-programming projects, router-configuration labs, deep queueing-theory math, SDN controller implementation, and advanced wireless/cellular PHY internals are beyond this course's depth.
key_topics: Analog/digital signals, bandwidth, and signal impairment
Link-layer framing, CRC error detection, and CSMA/CD Ethernet
ARP and MAC vs IP addressing
IP datagram format, subnetting, CIDR, and NAT
TCP three-way handshake, reliable transfer, flow and congestion control (AIMD, slow start)
BitTorrent P2P and video streaming basics
one_liner: Undergraduate computer-networking fundamentals taught top-to-bottom across the TCP/IP stack (physical, link, network, transport, application) plus a brief VPN unit — does NOT include socket programming labs, router/switch configuration, SDN implementation, or advanced wireless PHY/cellular depth.
